articles.title: Ombudsman: Godolphin great set for Japan Cup swansong
articles.summary: Champion Stakes hero Ombudsman is set for one final start in the Japan Cup before being retired to stud, trainer John Gosden has confirmed; The Godolphin-owned star, who is the back-to-back winner of the Prince Of Wales's Stakes, missed out on a trip to the Breeders' Cup last month.
articles.body:
Joint-trainers John and Thady Gosden elected against a Breeders' Cup run for the son of Night Of Thunder after his victory in the Champion Stakes, but he will now tackle a mile and a half for the first time in Tokyo on November 29 before stallion duties await at Darley's Kildangan Stud in Ireland in 2027.

However, win, lose or draw in the Far East, Godolphin's managing director Hugh Anderson believes his legacy has already been secured and he will go down as "one of the best" to represent Sheikh Mohammed's operation on the racetrack.

He told the Press Association: "John is a master trainer and has obviously got his eye very firmly on this prize. It's very exciting.

"Ombudsman's career has been a model of his kind and he has been beautifully trained. John really took his time with him both as a two-year-old and a three-year-old and what rewards we reaped as a result.

"There have been a lot of great racehorses in Godolphin's history but Ombudsman is one of the best because of the quality of the Group Ones he has won.

"There is a pecking order in this sport and there are not many higher ranking than two Prince of Wales's Stakes at Royal Ascot, the Juddmonte International Stakes and a Champion Stakes, he's right up there."

Ombudsman is likely to face his old foe and defending champion Calandagan in Japan as the five-time Group One winner attempts to become the first British-trained winner since Alkaased 21 years ago and also land a $5million bonus he is eligible for after his recent Ascot strike.

The Clarehaven star proved too much for Francis-Henri Graffard's globetrotter on Champions Day and although the Sheikh Mohammed-owned Singspiel tasted Japan Cup glory in 1996, he would become the first horse to win the Group One in the Godolphin silks if repeating the dose in Asia.

It would be a result that would cap what has turned into a fine year for the global operation, who have recently seen Sovereignty provide them with a first Breeders' Cup Classic in Keeneland on the back of a strong end to the European season that provides plenty of optimism for 2027.

"The Breeders' Cup Classic really was something and like Ombudsman, Sovereignty is out there in a class of his own," continued Anderson.

"He has won two of the massive international races that had never been previously won by Godolphin or His Highness - the Kentucky Derby and the Breeders' Cup Classic. For one horse to do both is seriously impressive and he will be a fabulous stallion."

He went on: "The year is ending strongly and I have been on record saying it was a little bit flat earlier in the year - and it was always going to be difficult to match the quality of last year, but we have finished well.

"The two-year-olds have been very good this year and I think Charlie Appleby has shown how good a trainer he is to bring along the likes of Talk Of New York to win a Queen Elizabeth II Stakes at the end of the season.

"He is going to be an exciting older horse and while there are the likes of Ombudsman and Notable Speech moving off the roster, he is one to take us onwards next year alongside the likes of Opera Ballo and some very good two-year-olds - I'm very optimistic about 2027."

articles.title: Formula 1 proceeding with plans to finish 2026 season in Middle East as deadline to hold race at Imola passes
articles.summary: Formula 1 chiefs informed organisers at Imola that the Italian circuit will not be required for use at the end of the 2026 season; the historic track had been on standby to stage a race in the event F1 felt its final two rounds could not safely be staged in Qatar and Abu Dhabi
articles.body:
F1 had to cancel races scheduled in April in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia due to conflict in the Middle East, which has continued throughout the year to cast doubt over the final two rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.

A contingency plan had been arranged for Imola to host a season-ending race in the first week of December, but those in charge at the Italian circuit were informed on Tuesday that it will not be needed, which confirms F1's intention to go ahead with the final two rounds as planned.

The Qatar Grand Prix is scheduled for November 27-29, with the Abu Dhabi Grand Prix set to follow from December 4-6. The races complete a triple-header that starts with the Las Vegas Grand Prix from November 20-22.

F1 president Stefano Domenicali has maintained throughout the season that the final races would be held at their scheduled venues unless the situation in the Middle East deteriorated.

The Italian has also insisted the safety of everyone involved in F1 remains his priority, and it is understood the sport's bosses wouldn't hesitate to cancel the races should the situation change over the coming weeks.

The sport's teams and drivers have repeatedly expressed trust in F1's judgement on the situation, and there has been no suggestion that any of the 11 squads are against completing the season as planned.

The season is set to fall just one short of it's original 24-race schedule, with the Bahrain Grand Prix having been rescheduled and hosted by Malaysia in October.

The Lusail International Circuit, which hosts the Qatar Grand Prix, staged a round of the MotoGP season from November 6-8.

There had been security concerns ahead of the event, which led to Japanese constructor Yamaha opting not to attend, but it passed without incident.

Kimi Antonelli sealed the F1 drivers' title in Mexico City before his Mercedes team closed out the constructors' title a week later in Brazil.

Ben Sulayem: We are ready for Qatar and Abu Dhabi

FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem posted on social media on Tuesday insisting that the sport's governing body is "fully prepared" for the final two rounds of the season.

"We are ready for Qatar and Abu Dhabi," Ben Sulayem wrote on Instagram.

"We are fully prepared and committed to delivering two outstanding Grands Prix weekends and a spectacular conclusion to the FIA Formula One World Championship.

"We look forward to welcoming drivers, teams and fans to two iconic circuits for an unforgettable finish to the season.

articles.standfirst: En Brasil se rodó en mojado y no pasó nada. Hay que confiar en los pilotos, pero no en lo que dicen por la radio bajo la lluvia
articles.summary: En Brasil se rodó en mojado y no pasó nada. Hay que confiar en los pilotos, pero no en lo que dicen por la radio bajo la lluvia
articles.body: Interlagos me reconcilió con la Fórmula 1. Estaba hasta las narices de que se esperara a que no cayera una gota para dar luz verde a una calificación o carrera. De hecho, el pasado sábado parecían ir por el mismo camino. Intentaron arrancar, pero el cielo se abrió y hubo que parar. Y así, durante una larga hora. Imágenes repetidas de otras veces, el coche de seguridad que sale a revisar la pista, pilotos que se suben y tienen que bajarse a continuación de los coches, bromas forzadas ante la cámara, sonrisas fingidas... ...Pero las previsiones eran inciertas para el domingo por la mañana y el director de carrera Rui Marques decidió iniciar la Q1 por el riesgo de quedarse sin luz. La pista estaba más o menos como quince minutos antes, y pronto llegaron las quejas por radio de las estrellas del Mundial. Ni caso, hay que ignorar sus comentarios, y quedarse con lo bueno que son subidos a los monoplazas. No hubo ningún accidente de gravedad. Nada más bajarse del coche, George Russell alertó de que las condiciones eran límite para la carrera. No es ese el camino. Salgan detrás del coche de seguridad con ruedas de mucha agua y, si hay agarre suficiente, tiren. La cortina de agua y la visibilidad son entonces el problema, pero mayor es el daño que se hace el espectáculo si la Fórmula 1 deja de sentirse como un desafío. En la carrera del domingo les vimos rodar con ruedas blandas de seco sobre mojado. Si el circuito es suficientemente seguro hay que intentarlo. No puede ser que el miedo de Spa, donde correr bajo la lluvia ya no existe, se apodere de todos los escenarios del Mundial. Tampoco estoy de acuerdo con las medidas de mitigación del calor en los coches. Chalecos refrigerantes, entradas de aire adicionales... Eso era inconcebible en el pasado. Para eso están tan en forma. Un piloto exhausto es la prueba de que este deporte sigue siendo un desafío. Todo lo que pueda generar incertidumbre o errores de pilotaje debe ser aplaudido. En Qatar 26 volverá a activarse el protocolo de altas temperaturas. El desencadenante fue la carrera de Losail de hace tres años. El aire era asfixiante. Hubo mareos, varios acabaron al borde del desmayo. Fueron héroes. La seguridad debe estar por encima de todo. Desde la muerte de Jules Bianchi en 2014 el celo es máximo, y hay que aplaudirlo, pero el automovilismo es un deporte de riesgo. Intentarlo en Brasil mereció la pena. Nos dio un fin de semana de carreras memorable. Con el aroma clásico de Interlagos, una pista de valientes y de buenos pilotos.

articles.title: Formula 1: Season to finish in Qatar and Abu Dhabi as planned
articles.summary: The 2026 Formula 1 season will conclude with the Qatar and Abu Dhabi grands prix as planned, with Italy's Imola circuit stood down as back-up for the races.
articles.body:
Formula 1 has told the Imola circuit in Italy that it will not be required as a back-up for the two end-of-season races in the Middle East.

The sport is pressing ahead with plans to hold the two events in Qatar on 27-29 November and Abu Dhabi in the United Arab Emirates on 4-6 December, despite the ongoing conflict between the United States/Israel and Iran.

Imola had been asked to prepare for a potential grand prix on the Abu Dhabi dates if the two Middle Eastern races could not go ahead.

Imola was asked on Tuesday to stand down preparations - but F1 says that if the situation in the Middle East deteriorates it is still prepared to cancel the two races.

Earlier in the season, races in Saudi Arabia and Bahrain, both of which had been scheduled for April, were cancelled and delayed respectively following the outbreak of the United States and Israel's war with Iran.

The Bahrain Grand Prix was eventually held at Malaysia's Sepang circuit in October.

"If the situation develops negatively in the coming weeks before the events in the Middle East, we will not hesitate to do the right thing and the safety of everyone will always be the priority," an F1 spokesperson said on Tuesday.

F1 says the decision to press ahead with Qatar and Abu Dhabi, which was always the default option, has been taken because the situation in the two countries has not "negatively developed" in recent months.

Travel advice from governments still allows travel, insurance is valid, events are taking place and business has returned to a normal level in both countries, it said, adding that the teams are all supportive of concluding the season as planned.

A MotoGP race was held in Qatar last weekend. That sport is owned by the same US group that owns F1.

Despite the decision, a number of senior figures in F1 have expressed disquiet to BBC Sport about the idea of going to the Middle East for the races, as both are close to areas in the Straight of Hormuz where missile strikes are still taking place.

And Saudi Arabia continues to be the target of attacks from Houthi rebels in Yemen.

Several events in Saudi Arabia, which borders Qatar and the United Arab Emirates, have been cancelled or postponed in recent weeks following those attacks.

However, there is recognition that F1 faces a difficult decision. The two countries pay large fees for their events, and both are heavily ingrained in the fabric of the sports as sponsors and investors.

The Qatari sovereign investment fund, for example, is a part owner of the Audi team, and Abu Dhabi is the same for McLaren.

articles.title: Sao Paulo GP: Martin Brundle's verdict as Mercedes seal 2026 F1 constructors' title and Lando Norris wins wet race in Brazil
articles.summary: Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle gives his verdict as Lando Norris triumphs on wet weekend at Sao Paulo Grand Prix and Mercedes seal the 2026 Constructors' Championship
articles.body:
I must first congratulate the whole Mercedes Benz team, car and power unit combined, for once again winning the Constructors' Championship for a ninth time as a team.

A tally which draws team boss Toto Wolff level with Sir Frank Willams as the most in F1 history, and with a further eight Mercedes drivers' titles on his watch, equalling Sir Ron Dennis' combined total of 17 as team principal. That's outstanding company in the hierarchy of F1. Well done to every person concerned.

Driver of the weekend for me was Lando Norris, although we didn't have the chance to witness the full extent of Max Verstappen's talents, more of which later. Max was voted the fans' driver of the day for the sixth time in the last seven races.

There has been relatively little wet running in the all-new 2026 cars, Sepang notwithstanding, and none in Interlagos until the 'qualifying hour', which took a total of 146 minutes to conclude, with Lando on pole position.

The rain fell heavily and the cars floated around even on full wet tyres, and so it had to be red flagged for a good while. Luckily there was a window here and there to get the whole process done, even if the last six minutes on a once more saturated track understandably saw no action.

George Russell was aggrieved he didn't 'win' qualifying before he took his five-place grid penalty for needing an extra internal combustion engine over and above the annual allowance. George came across Alex Albon's Williams during a small window in the level of water on the track, and together with his pit wall decided to abandon that lap and make some space for a final effort, but it was too wet. If they had continued, there's a chance it would have been provisional pole, and George needs every ounce of good news he can find at the moment.

He was in fine form all weekend, saying he felt like his old self despite the conditions, but a spin in the pit lane after his first stop in the race may well be the image which sums up his year. He'll bounce back, I have no doubt.

Through all the trials and tribulations emerged Lando in his upgraded McLaren, the only team to have new parts in Brazil as the season heads towards conclusion. The track had been resurfaced in places too, and it was a mission to find the best grip whilst not dismantling the car against the barriers.

The higher ride height and more supple 2026 cars looked quite controllable in the conditions as it turned out, but the skills on show were impressive to say the least.

Rafael Camara had a baptism of fire on his F1 debut for the Haas team, in Esteban Ocon's seat, at his home Grand Prix. He clouted the turn three exit barriers hard in Q1 but survived to make Q2, where he once again made it nose first into the turn 12 barriers on the cruel downhill wet grass. In the race, he would cross the line 20th and in last place, having achieved seven of the overall 22 track limit infringements, but at least he saw the flag, albeit two laps down.

Verstappen was taking a host of power unit penalties and guaranteed to start from the back of the grid and so only participated in the first part of qualifying. Saving some of the precious rain tyres, limited to two sets of full wets and five sets of intermediate tyres for the whole weekend, was paramount given that the race was expected to be wet.

From 21st and the back row, Max would carve through many cars even before the exit of turn three, including Charles Leclerc who started his Ferrari in 14th. We then witnessed another Max special as he finished second at the flag, beaten only by Lando on imperious form.

It must be said that his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar had a fine race too for the final spot on the podium. He was asked to move over for the flying Verstappen at one point and then appeared to hang onto his gearbox with relative ease, although at the finish he was 9.8 seconds behind his team leader, who was similarly 14.6 seconds behind Lando.

With Oscar Piastri finishing down in sixth place after pitting a lap too late for the final set of intermediate tyres once the rain kicked in again on lap 61 of 71, this meant that McLaren and Red Bull earned 33 points each in their battle for third in the Constructors', which is advantage Red Bull heading into the final three races.

Kimi Antonelli led the opening stages on intermediates after an excellent start, but as soon as he went onto dry tyres on lap 17 his race began to unravel. Struggling for warm-up of the tyres and therefore confidence too, he spun off in the first corner and flat spotted his tyres, which handed the lead to Lando before he then quickly came under pressure from both Red Bulls.

Like George in the sister Mercedes, he was experiencing a weird feeling in the car of something broken and pulling one way, and that remained a mystery to the team even at the airport later that evening. Perhaps it was a mismatch of tyre temperatures and pressures, perhaps the unique track layout and surfacing, including the numerous sections diamond cut to aid drainage and reduce aquaplaning.

Russell had a strong and very long middle stint, such that pitting for intermediate tyres on lap 61 meant he undid some of the lost time from that pit-exit spin to end up fourth and ahead of his newly-crowned world champion team-mate Antonelli in fifth.

In true Interlagos chaotic style, this meant the only time a Mercedes driver was on the podium post-race was for the team's Constructors' Championship celebrations.

Lewis Hamilton, like Verstappen, had a tremendous start from 20th on the grid and moved swiftly forward. However, his starting intermediate tyres seem less happy than most and he was first over the radio to urgently want to pit, and indeed to pit, on lap 14.

Lewis had read early that it was time for dry tyres, although I'm led to believe he was reluctant to pit for intermediates later on which meant a high-speed spin in heading to the pits on lap 62 in the now heavier rain, during which he was lucky not to tear the rear wing off. This meant he was consigned to ninth place at the finish, a lap down.

Ahead of him in eighth was Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc, who had a strangely anonymous race lacking grip until the final phase on intermediate tyres, which allowed him to pass Niko Hulkenberg and Liam Lawson.

However, during his tussle with Lawson, he nudged the Racing Bulls' rear wheel at turn 12 which attracted a five-second penalty, which in turn elevated Lawson back up to seventh.

Lawson put in yet another strong performance for Racing Bulls, running as high as second in the early stages, to further complicate their decision on driver line up for next season. He's been on fire since returning to the team having substituted for the injured Hadjar in the senior Red Bull team.

That concluded a breathless six F1 races in seven weekends, with a slight breather now before a Las Vegas, Qatar, and Abu Dhabi triple-header to finish the season.

articles.title: La FIA descarta correr en Imola y confirma que se disputarán las citas de Qatar y Abu Dhabi
articles.standfirst: No se cumplirá el plan B en el calendario del Mundial de Fórmula 1 2026. Ben Sulayem, presidente de la FIA, ha confirmado que "están listos" para que se celebren ambos eventos
articles.summary: No se cumplirá el plan B en el calendario del Mundial de Fórmula 1 2026. Ben Sulayem, presidente de la FIA, ha confirmado que "están listos" para que se celebren ambos eventos
articles.body: a nadie puede sorprender que se vaya a correr finalmente en Qatar y Abu Dhabi. Existía un indicio que eliminaba cualquier atisbo de duda. El pasado fin de semana se acabó disputando el evento de MotoGP en el recinto de Lusail. Así que todo apuntaba a que el de Fórmula 1 también se iba a mantener, tal y como ha confirmado este martes el presidente de la FIA, Mohammed Ben Sulayem, en su cuenta de Instagram. "Estamos preparados para celebrar las citas de Qatar y Abu Dhabi. Estamos totalmente comprometidos y preparados para ofrecer dos grandes fines de semana y un final espectacular para el Mundial 2026 de Fórmula 1", ha subrayado el mandamás del organismo rector de la categoría reina del automovilismo. "Estamos deseando dar la bienvenida a los pilotos, los equipos y los aficionados a estos dos circuitos emblemáticos para vivir un final de temporada inolvidable. Nos vemos en la parrilla", ha apostillado Ben Sulayem, quien de manera implícita ha descartado la opción de Imola, una sede que había sonado como alternativa si es que finalmente los otros trazados eran descartados por motivos de seguridad. Por ende, salvo que la situación bélica empeore en Oriente Medio, el final del certamen se mantendrá como estaba previsto. La primera parada será la semana que viene en Las Vegas (del 19 al 21 de noviembre). Una semana después se disputará el Gran Premio de Qatar (del 27 al 29 del presente mes) y en Abu Dhabi caerá el telón ya en diciembre (del 4 al 6). En retrospectiva, los rectores de la F1 han sido capaces de mantener el calendario casi completo (23 citas de las 24 iniciales). Eso sí, la guerra de Estados Unidos e Israel contra Irán provocaron en su momento que se cancelara la ronda de Arabia Saudí. Además, los organizadores del Gran Circo decidieron aplazar el evento que debía tener lugar en Bahréin también por la delicada situación geopolítica en Oriente Medio. Meses después (en concreto en octubre) se disputó en Sepang. Fue una medida algo extraña, ya que la carrera mantuvo el nombre del país árabe, pero se celebró a miles de kilómetros de distancia. Así fue como el circuito malasio volvió a la F1 casi una década después.

articles.title: Ferrari should back 'extraordinary' Lewis Hamilton over Charles Leclerc as number one driver, Damon Hill tells Sky Sports' The F1 Show
articles.summary: Catch up on all the major talking points from the Sao Paulo GP by listening to the latest episode of The F1 Show podcast; Damon Hill and Anthony Davidson join Simon Lazenby to discuss Ferrari's issues, Mercedes' completing their title double, and Lando Norris' victory in Brazil
articles.body:
Ferrari's handling of their drivers came under increased scrutiny earlier this month following the Mexico City Grand Prix when a first-lap clash between Hamilton and Leclerc, running in first and second respectively at the time, cost the Italian team a likely one-two, with Red Bull's Max Verstappen going on to win the race.

Hamilton, who had started on pole and led on the approach to the first corner, was highly critical of Leclerc after the race for what he perceived to be an overly aggressive approach against a team-mate. Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur also expressed his displeasure at the incident.

The seven-time world champion said any issues he had with Leclerc had been "squashed" following a conversation at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, which came the weekend after the race in Mexico.

Hill, the 1996 world champion, wrote on social media following the race in Mexico that Italian squad should make Hamilton their number one driver for the 2027 season and that "Lewis will deliver for Ferrari if they back him 100 per cent."

Appearing on the latest episode of Sky Sports' The F1 Show following the triple-header of races, Hill explained his position.

"They [Ferrari] have invested all this in Lewis, they've got him on board, he is a massive name in the sport," the 1996 world champion said.

"If they have a competitive car next year, they could win the Drivers' Championship and the Constructors' Championship, and I can't see how they're going to win it if they have two drivers currently behaving the way they do, if Charles is constantly racing against Lewis like that.

"So, you have to make a decision as a team principal how you're going to enter into the fray. And I think it makes sense to me to put all your eggs behind Lewis.

"You've got him there anyway. You've gone through all the pain and the investment to get him there. It would be a huge story, clearly. His eighth world title is just sitting there.

"Now Charles might say, well, this is totally unfair, you know, I've been here longer. But yes, you have been there longer, but look at the results.

"Lewis has got a valid point, which is he's there to make them win as a team, not just be a Ferrari driver."

'Hamilton has rebuilt himself after being crushed by 2021 title loss'

After claiming the most recent of his seven titles in 2020, Hamilton was controversially denied a record eighth triumph as he lost out to Max Verstappen at the final race of the 2021 season.

That coincided with a drop-off in performance for the Mercedes team that Hamilton had won six of his seven titles with, which ultimately played a part in the Brit deciding to make a blockbuster switch to Ferrari for the 2025 season.

Hamilton's last campaign with Mercedes and first with Ferrari suggested he was on the decline as he was outperformed by former team-mate George Russsell and then Leclerc, but he has returned to form in 2026.

With the all-new cars for this season appearing to better suit him, Hamilton claimed his first grand prix victory for Ferrari in Barcelona to reignite hope he could once more contend for the title.

Leclerc, who spent just one season at Sauber before joining Ferrari as a 21-year-old, has claimed nine grand prix wins across his eight campaigns with the Italian team.

Hill added: "I think there's a gravitas that Lewis has. I mean, don't forget what he was like last year. He was crushed.

"He's been crushed since Abu Dhabi, in effect, you know, in 2021. He's been fighting his way back. He's performed incredibly well this year, much better than I thought, considering I thought it was going to be very difficult, but he's rebuilt himself.

"He is an extraordinary individual. And I think he has, and he's got pole positions and won races this year in a Ferrari. Who would have said that was possible last year?

"And I think we need to settle this in the team because there's a political problem in that team. For me, it seems like there's factions within the team that are shooting for one side or the other.

"You can't have that if you're going to be an effective competitor against the Red Bulls, McLaren and Mercedes."

Davidson: Number one status has to be earned

Sky Sports F1 pundit Anthony Davidson, appearing on The F1 Show alongside Hill, questioned whether Hamilton has earned number one status over Leclerc at Ferrari.

Hamilton is fourth in the 2026 drivers' standings, a place ahead of Leclerc with just 12 points separating the pair.

Davidson compared the situation to that of Verstappen at Red Bull, where the four-time world champion has long received preferential treatment over his team-mates.

Davidson said: "Do you think, though, with Red Bull, that it's not like they give Max better equipment? He has, without question, earned that status in the team through his dominance of lap times alone.

"And it's pretty much every time. A bit like [Michael] Schumacher did against either [Rubens] Barrichello or [Felipe] Massa or [Eddie] Irvine.

"It was just every time he is unbeatable. And you earn that. You have to earn that status.

"I'm not comfortable with the fact, thinking of Charles, the speed he had particularly last year. I wouldn't be comfortable with the fact if you just say the number one in the team is Lewis and Charles, no matter where he is, you finish behind.

"That doesn't sit easy with me. I think to a certain degree, you have to earn that status in the team."

articles.title: 22-Year-Old Jockey Izzy Neale Dies After Fall During Race in Australia
articles.summary: Australian apprentice jockey Izzy Neale has died at age 22 after her horse suffered a fatal fall in a Sunday race in Australia, her family announced.
articles.body:
Australian apprentice jockey Izzy Neale has died at age 22 after her horse suffered a fatal fall in a Sunday race in Australia, her family announced.

The news was shared by Racing NSW, which regulates thoroughbred horse racing in New South Wales.

"It is with deep sadness and broken hearts that we announce the passing of our beloved Izzy, surrounded by her closest family and friends," Neale's family stated. "Izzy rode horses before she could walk. Her love of horses was a lifelong passion that, more recently, had grown into a love of racing.

"Through organ donation, Izzy will give others the chance of life, bringing some comfort to our family amid this devastating loss."

Neale fell from her horse, Marnoo, during the one-mile Warren Shire Cotton Cup on Sunday in New South Wales.

She was airlifted to Dubbo Hospital in critical condition . Her brother later said in a social media post Neale had been placed on life support.

Marnoo was euthanized after suffering a near foreleg injury, according to Racing NSW .

Jockey Diego Montes de Oca, who was injured at the same point in the race, was released from the hospital with soft tissue injuries to his left foot, according to Racing NSW .

Neale was a native of Merriwa, New South Wales, who graduated from the picnic to professional circuit. She earned her first picnic win in February 2024 and went on to record 88 career wins and 269 places in 699 starts.

She had celebrated her first metropolitan winner with It's A Tata this July at Rosehill Gardens outside Sydney.

Racing NSW previously announced a race scheduled for Monday in Scone, located near Neale's hometown, would be rescheduled to Wednesday.

articles.title: Kyle Busch posthumously voted most popular driver in the NASCAR Cup Series for 2026
articles.summary: Busch’s widow, Samantha, was on hand to accept the posthumous trophy at the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts.
articles.body:
MIAMI — The late Kyle Busch was recognized as the Cup Series' most popular driver Tuesday at NASCAR's season-ending awards banquet.

Busch's widow, Samantha, was on hand to accept the posthumous trophy at the Adrienne Arsht Center for the Performing Arts. It was the first time Busch was honored with the award in a 25-year NASCAR career that spanned all three national series.

He died at age 41 in May after severe pneumonia progressed into sepsis, resulting in rapid and overwhelming complications. His death stunned the NASCAR community, which responded with weekly tributes to the two-time series champion (2015, 2019).

Chase Elliott of Hendrick Motorsports had won the previous eight most popular driver awards in the Cup Series, but he asked the National Motorsports Press Association to remove him from consideration in 2026.

Busch became the first driver not named Earnhardt or Elliott to win the fan vote since Darrell Waltrip in 1990.

"There has been so much love for Kyle from this sport over the past several months, and I wish more than anything that he could be here to see it," Samantha Busch said. "He gave so much of his life to racing and I know it would mean the world to him to see the impact he had on NASCAR and the people who love it.

"Kyle never changed who he was to make people like him. He was passionate, outspoken and fiercely competitive. He was Rowdy through and through. Whether you cheered him or booed him, he gave you something to make noise about and he loved that. To Kyle, that passion is what made this sport so special. Seeing that same passion bring everyone together to honor him has been incredible."

Samantha Busch thanked all the drivers who encouraged their fans to vote for her husband and said that respect from the drivers he raced against meant so much. She closed her remarks directing her comments toward the fans.

"And to the fans, I wish you knew just how much you meant to him. ... There was no Rowdy without the fans," she said referring to her husband's nickname. "There will never be another Rowdy because there is truly no one else like Kyle."

Bill Elliott won every year between 1991 and 2000. Dale Earnhardt was posthumously awarded the title following his on-track death in 2001.

Elliott picked up the trophy again in 2002, then Dale Earnhardt Jr. started a 15-year run that ended with his retirement from full-time racing in 2017. Chase Elliott took it from there.

Busch won 234 times across NASCAR's top three national series — the most of any driver in history — and he is considered a first ballot Hall of Famer.

articles.title: Bezzecchi, el rey... sin los Sprint: “Habría firmado un año como este”
articles.standfirst: Sería primero si sólo se contaran los puntos del domingo, aunque dice que no eliminaría las carreras cortas ni ve malo el 2026 que está haciendo
articles.summary: Sería primero si sólo se contaran los puntos del domingo, aunque dice que no eliminaría las carreras cortas ni ve malo el 2026 que está haciendo
articles.body: Alguno se preguntará por qué Massimo Rivola, CEO de Aprilia Racing, planteaba un cambio en el sistema de puntuación de MotoGP. Los datos, lógicamente, dan la respuesta. MARCA constató que si sólo se miraran los puntos logrados por cada uno de los tres participantes que siguen en liza por el Mundial, Marc Márquez, Jorge Martín y Marco Bezzecchi... el que tendría más sería el competidor italiano de la casa de Noale. Después de la prueba de Qatar, el de Rímini sumaría 277 puntos, frente a los 267 del leridano y los 252 del madrileño. Por lo tanto, queda claro cuál ha sido el punto débil de ‘Bez’ esta campaña: las carreras cortas. De hecho, no ha ganado ninguna de las 20 que se han celebrado, pues en Australia sí se disputó ésta, pero no la larga; por el contrario, el del Ducati oficial se ha impuesto hasta en diez. Pese a ello, el transalpino no es favorable a quitar estas carreras. “Me gustaría mejorarlos en lugar de eliminarlos. He conseguido siete podios en sprints, pero el problema es que también he cometido muchos pequeños errores y he tenido mucha mala suerte. Necesito pulir algunos detalles”, afirmaba en Sky. Para algunos, Bezzecchi ha sido el que ha perdido este Mundial, pues tenía una ventaja de 102 puntos frente al de Cervera, tras Mugello, que era la séptima prueba de este 2026, pero Marco sorprendía al considerar que no está siendo una temporada tan decepcionante. En Sky le preguntaron directamente si firmaría un año como el que ha vivido y no lo dudó. “Sí, habría firmado. Mi objetivo era empezar de la mejor manera posible, teniendo en cuenta que el año pasado tuvimos dificultades en la primera mitad de la temporada. Quería empezar con fuerza, y lo conseguí. Es cierto que a mitad de temporada hubo algunas carreras en las que, por una razón u otra, las cosas no salieron como esperábamos. Las lesiones también influyeron. Después volvimos a la senda del triunfo y conseguimos varios podios; volví a ganar en Indonesia y también en Qatar. Ha sido una temporada fantástica hasta ahora, aunque los sprints han sido mi punto débil, pero se trata de ganar experiencia y tratar de mejorar”, proclamó. No es exactamente lo que piensa Rivola, que cree que su pupilo ha sido “el más rápido”, con lo que la lamentación es clara entre los del Norte de Italia. “Es una pena que con esa velocidad no nos se lleve muchas veces todo el botín”, exponía el dirigente en Sky. Sin embargo, lo que parece evidente es que ‘Bez’ ha errado en demasiadas ocasiones, ya fuera los sábados o los domingos. Eso lo certifica hasta Valentino Rossi, su mentor en la Academia de la que forma parte. “Bezzecchi está bien porque ganó en Qatar, pero está un poco decepcionado porque este año tenía la posibilidad de ganar el Mundial, tenía la velocidad, pero ha cometido demasiados errores y, probablemente, no lo conseguirá”, confesaba El Doctor en el programa ‘Che tempo che fa’, de la televisión de su país, cuando presentó su biografía... y siguió con su mantra de críticas a Marc Márquez por 2015.

articles.title: Sainz aprieta a Pirelli por los neumáticos de lluvia: "Necesitan mejorar"
articles.standfirst: El piloto de Williams pondera la situación que se vivió con los neumáticos durante la carrera disputada en Interlagos
articles.summary: El piloto de Williams pondera la situación que se vivió con los neumáticos durante la carrera disputada en Interlagos
articles.body: Cada Gran Premio, una de las batallas más importantes a las cada equipo tiene que hacer frente es la elección de los neumáticos y la gestión de éstos a lo largo del fin de semana. Sin embargo, la historia cambia cuando la meteorología decide ser parte de la fiesta, entonces, la gestión de los compuestos se vuelve un auténtico quebradero de cabeza. Además, si le suma las condiciones mixtas que se han vivido durante el Gran Premio de Brasil de F1 este fin de semana, elegir el neumático correcto sí que se vuelve un deporte de alto riesgo, pues de acertar o equivocarse dependerá la carrera por completo. Desde su entrada al Mundial de F1 como proveedor oficial de neumáticos en 2009, y cuyo contrato ha sido extendido, por el momento, hasta 2028, Pirelli muestra un amplia gama de neumáticos, cinco para seco, de los cuales tres son elegidos por el fabricante dependiendo del circuito para ofrecérselo a los equipos, y dos para mojado, lo cual ha supuesto un problema durante el fin de semana en Interlagos. Ante un fin de semana el cual ya se presentaba con condiciones de mojado la mayor parte del tiempo, Pirelli no cambió sus opciones de neumáticos de lluvia: verde para lluvia ligera, ofreciendo un total de 4 juegos por piloto, y azul para lluvia extrema, 3 juegos por piloto. No obstante, el problema no viene tanto de la cantidad de los neumáticos, sino más bien de la calidad, especialmente cuando se habla de la degradación que estos pueden llegar a tener. Y es que, desde su entrada en la F1, los equipos han aprendido a gestionar los juegos de neumáticos 'slicks' que tienen cada fin de semana, dependiendo de la degradación que la pista pueda presentar. Sin embargo, cuando la lluvia empieza a formar parte de la función, esa degradación y esa gestión se vuelve mucho más complicada, al no tener tantos escenarios donde ponerlo en práctica. Es por ello que, tras una carrera de condiciones mixtas donde la pista comenzó muy mojada, se secó rápidamente y luego volvió a mojarse durante los últimos tramos de la sesión, acertar con el neumático fue un auténtico infierno, pues pusieran el compuesto que pusieran, iba a dar problemas. Y fue así justo lo que sucedió, pues muchos fueron los pilotos que se quejaron de esa alta degradación que sufrieron con los neumáticos intermedios a medida que la pista se iba secando. "Creo que el rendimiento de los neumáticos de lluvia y los intermedios no es lo suficientemente bueno, y tenemos que trabajar con Pirelli para encontrar un neumático mejor, porque en condiciones mixtas el neumático intermedio sigue siendo muy débil en la parte trasera", declaraba el piloto español de Williams, Carlos Sainz, uno de los que más sufrió esa degradación. Del mismo modo, el madrileño añadió precisamente esas dificultades en las que la pista no está para 'inters', porque se destrozan rápidamente, pero tampoco para 'slicks', porque la pista está lo suficientemente mojada como para perder el coche en cualquier acción. "Para cuando empiece a hacer calor, el frente ya se habrá ido. Y, sinceramente, tuvimos mucho aquaplaning y una gran falta de agarre trasero. Así que a estos dos neumáticos aún les falta un poco de desarrollo. No sé...", sentenciaba Sainz.

articles.title: James Vowles: Williams boss admits team got carried away with success but says 2026 F1 season struggles are only 'a blip'
articles.summary: Watch or listen to the latest episode of The Fast and the Curious to hear Williams boss James Vowles discuss the team's 2026 struggles, why he is confident a corner has been turned, and the changes he wants to see made to F1's cost cap rules
articles.body:
Vowles took charge of Williams after joining from Mercedes at the start of 2023 and appeared to be having a hugely positive impact when the team finished fifth in the 2025 constructors' standings, which was their best finish since 2017.

However, the biggest regulation change in the sport's history, which saw the introduction of both new power units and chassis, has seen Williams regress, leaving drivers Carlos Sainz and Alex Albon hugely frustrated.

They are ninth of the 11 teams with three rounds of the 2026 season remaining and have scored just 12 points, which compares poorly to a final total of 137 a year earlier.

Appearing on the latest episode of The Fast and the Curious podcast, Vowles said: "There's going to be blips in the pathway. This is what I consider a blip, unfortunately.

"And I think it's a good thing we went through it because we've made some pretty enormous changes in the backside of the team, which we had to go through, in my opinion, to make the next steps.

"And I think we got carried away a little bit with ourselves last year, demonstrating that actually when things aren't changing too much, we have the ability to produce a half decent car. But regulation changes will always expose you."

Despite Williams' struggles leading to speculation over the security of Vowles' job, the 47-year-old insists that he is not feeling the pressure.

"When I signed up to this, I had an agreement with the board that we're going to find some horrible things when we start pushing ourselves," Vowles said. "It's not a business where we can go out there and completely predict where we're going to be in different phases.

"But I will dedicate my heart, soul and every hour of my day, as will the team into fixing it when we find it. But I ask in return that there's a support behind us in that way.

"And I have to say that the board has been outstanding, really, to the extent where I remember in winter, a pretty horrible time in winter, I was working seven day weeks and 16-hour, 18-hour days, it was hard. I called to see all of them. And all it was, was just really a 'we're here behind you. How can we help?' That was it.

"It is not an environment where people are taking this light-heartedly. They know that this is going to be a difficult challenge. I knew it was going to be a difficult challenge. My assurance to the world is everything we are doing is directionally correct for our future."

articles.title: Today on Sky Sports Racing: Jumps action from Bangor-on-Dee
articles.summary: In today’s feature, Mickey Bowen’s prolific Mighty Fleur looks to continue her winning streak, out to back up her four-timer as she tackles a competitive Listed contest at Bangor-on-Dee. They host seven races in all, live on Sky Sports Racing from 12.30pm.
articles.body:
1.00 Bangor-on-Dee - Progressive Mighty Fleur faces seven rivals

Mighty Fleur faces seven rivals as she heads up in class for this Listed Yorton Mares' Novices' Chase at Bangor.

The Mickey Bowen-trained six-year-old completed a four-timer when comfortably landing a Worcester handicap chase on her return from a break and she deserves a crack at this grade. The drop in trip is a concern, but she could not arrive in better health.

Siog Geal , winner of her sole point-to-point, showed a decent level over hurdles and finished runner-up at Chepstow when last seen in March. Rated 127, she looks an exciting recruit to fencing.

Jubilee Alpha was top-rated of these over hurdles but has lost her way a little and might be suited by a switch of yard and code, while recent winner Onefournine is another to note.

1.30 Bangor-on-Dee - First Confession and Jupiter Allen clash

First Confession and Jupiter Allen clash in a small but select field for this Weatherbys & Birdie Calendars Handicap Chase at 1.30pm.

Joe Tizzard fields First Confession who got off the mark over fences on his penultimate run before running down the field in the National Hunt Challenge Novices' Handicap Chase at the Cheltenham Festival. With the yard in good form, he rates a player from this two-pound lower mark.

Jupiter Allen dominated a decent field at Wincanton in January before failing to fire when pulled up in the Midlands National next time. Having made a low-key return over hurdles at Chepstow, he should strip fitter but would appreciate some rain.

Blenkisop built on his debut over fences to score at Exeter in November before struggling in a better race at Aintree. Not seen since December, he must be watched in the markets.

3.35 Bangor-on-Dee - Skelton's Brookside La takes on Charisma Cat

Brookside La bids to follow up in a trappy Festive Meeting Saturday 28th November Handicap Hurdle at 3.35pm.

Dan Skelton's charge doubled his tally over hurdles when winning by nine lengths at Worcester last month and, given the manner of that display, he ought to have more to give despite a nine-pound hike.

Alan King's Charisma Cat , a Listed bumper winner, enjoyed a fine first season over jumps winning on a couple of occasions before running a fair race to claim sixth against the boys in the Grade One Mersey Novices' Hurdle at Aintree. She will appreciate coming back into handicap company and must be respected under Tom Bellamy.

The Cistercian , Static and Good To Be Alive complete the quintet.

12.30 Bangor-on-Dee - Bowenspark and Laguna Beach headline. Wandering Ego could step up on his recent run.

2.05 Bangor - Rockson Piel is an interesting runner for Derham team.

2.35 Bangor - 91-rated Alcarath heads over hurdles.

articles.title: Tom O'Brien: Cheltenham Festival-winning jockey dies aged 39
articles.summary: Two-time Cheltenham Festival-winning jockey Tom O'Brien has passed away at the age of 39 following a lengthy battle with cancer; As a rider, O'Brien notched five Grade One successes before retiring in 2023.
articles.body:
O'Brien, who retired from the saddle in April 2023, rose to prominence with trainers Peter Bowen and Philip Hobbs and enjoyed a breakthrough season in 2006/07 with over 100 winners in that campaign.

The first of five Grade One successes came aboard Souffleur for Bowen in the 2007 Challow Novices' Hurdle, while later in his career O'Brien would strike up a memorable partnership with Hobbs' fan favourite Thyme Hill, landing the 2021 Liverpool Hurdle and 2022 Kauto Star Novices' Chase.

O'Brien also rode Dream Alliance to his against-all-odds victory in the 2009 Welsh Grand National, a story which would inspire a Hollywood film called Dream Horse.

Reflecting on O'Brien's life, Philip Hobbs said: "He came to our yard from Ireland having not ridden in a race, but it soon became obvious he was pretty talented and he was with us from the start of his career until the end.

"He was in the shadow of Richard Johnson for a long time being second jockey and then became first jockey after Richard retired, which went well. His biggest win was Thyme Hill in the Grade One at Aintree and he was always very reliable and a very good bloke.

"There's lots of good memories and there were lots of winners and I'd kept in touch with Tom since his retirement as he only lived half an hour away - he was only in our yard about three weeks ago.

"It's very sad, particularly for his wife Hayley and two young children."

Speaking on the Nick Luck Daily Podcast, Johnson White - now co-trainer with Philip Hobbs, said: "You couldn't get a harder working, nicer family man. I messaged Richard Johnson this morning and he sent a message back saying 'life is so cruel' and realistically you can't say any more than that. He leaves a lovely wife Hayley, two wonderful boys and a loving family that were there with him until the end."

Writing on Instagram, weighing room colleague Harry Cobden posted: "Gutted to hear the news about Tom. He was a great friend and a brilliant jockey. He will be hugely missed by everyone who knew him. Thoughts are with Hayley, Archie and Toby, and all his family and friends."

British Horseracing Authority (BHA) Chief Executive Brant Dunshea paid tribute, saying: "Tom was held in the highest esteem and meant so much to so many people across our sport, who benefitted from his kindness and loyal friendship.

"He touched countless lives on both sides of the Irish Sea, bringing joy to everyone who had the privilege of knowing him and watching what he did best, on and off the racecourse.

"He will be hugely missed and his loss is immensely difficult to process. The racing family is distraught, but I know how we will all rally round to provide each other with support, comfort and to remember Tom as we knew him best: a brilliant jockey, a valued colleague, a loyal friend and above all a loving husband and devoted father."

Trainer Christian Williams posted on X: "Kind, talented, humble and a true gentleman. Tom was a joy to be around and a privilege to have in the saddle. A friend to so many and of course, always smiling. Our thoughts and prayers are with Hayley, Archie, Toby, their families and many, many friends."

Writing on X, Sky Sports Racing broadcaster Mike Cattermole said: "Really saddened to hear about the passing of Tom O'Brien at 39. Obviously an excellent jockey but just a lovely guy, so gentle and humble. Thinking about all those who were close to him. Life is such a lottery."

articles.standfirst: 'Gigi' Dall'Igna elogia las capacidades de su piloto, aunque pide calma ante el trabajo que aún queda por hacer
articles.summary: 'Gigi' Dall'Igna elogia las capacidades de su piloto, aunque pide calma ante el trabajo que aún queda por hacer
articles.body: El CEO del equipo Ducati Lenovo, 'Gigi' Dall'Igna, califica a través de su LinkedIn el fin de semana en Qatar de sólido ante la "madurez, la experiencia y el talento de un auténtico campeón completo, capaz de marcar la diferencia siempre y en cualquier lugar". El italiano ha remarcado la importancia que ha acabado teniendo el Gran Premio de Qatar en la lucha del equipo por el título del Mundial de MotoGP en la que, a pesar de tenerlo muy de cara, aún queda rematar el trabajo. Tal y como lo refleja Dall'Igna, Marc Márquez pudo tirar una vez más de esa inteligencia que le caracteriza, especialmente desde que su estado físico cambió, y gestionar un fin de semana donde las Aprilia partían como favoritas. "Versátil como siempre, Marc sabe exactamente lo que hay que hacer y cómo adaptar sus habilidades, eligiendo el enfoque adecuado no solo para una carrera concreta, sino para ese momento exacto, con una visión aguda tanto de su propia situación como de la de sus rivales. Una lectura y una gestión magistrales de la carrera a medida que se desarrolla. ", explicaba el italiano. No obstante, y a pesar de la alegría que supuso la parte del box del '93', en el equipo de Borgo Panigale se quedan con un sabor agridulce del fin de semana pues, a pesar de la consistencia de Márquez, Bagnaia salió demasiado perjudicado. Tal y como explica Dall'Igna, el consistente fin de semana que volvía tener 'Pecco' no fue debidamente recompensado, algo que les causa mucho pesar y les afecta directamente: "Sin tener culpa alguna, salió disparado de repente de su moto. Un accidente violento, difícil de ver incluso por televisión, y diría que, afortunadamente, con consecuencias leves". Aun así, se alegran enormemente de haber podido ver de vuelta al campeón que es, y verle pelear por las primeras posiciones durante lo que duró su fin de semana, antes del accidente que le acarreó tal lesión. "Es un placer verle de vuelta en la pista así. Podría haber estado luchando con los pilotos más fuertes del grupo de cabeza, pero fue víctima de una fea colisión con otro piloto en las primeras vueltas de la carrera", afirmaba el gurú 'ducatista'. Del mismo modo, celebran a poca gravedad de la lesión ante lo que podría haber sido y desean tenerle lo antes posible en pista con el fin de darle la despedida que se merece al que, hasta ahora, sigue siendo el piloto más laureado de Ducati: "Estamos deseando verle de vuelta en el box para poder darle el abrazo y la despedida que se merece en estas dos últimas rondas de la temporada", concluía 'Gigi' En cuanto a la carrera, 'Gigi' la describe de poco emocionante pero necesaria para lo que será la carrera decisiva del Campeonato del Mundo de MotoGP. Tal y como explica el de Ducati, el '93' supo leer y gestionar la carrera dominical de tal manera que le dejara de cara el que será su 10º título, 8º en MotoGP: "La primera mitad se gestionó controlando el ritmo y el desgaste de los neumáticos, mientras que la segunda se caracterizó por un cambio de ritmo decisivo y emocionante, una remontada progresiva e implacable que, tras marcar la vuelta más rápida, le permitió asegurarse un preciadísimo segundo puesto. Logró sacar el máximo partido en una situación en la que no partía como favorito: un resultado excelente que se siente como una victoria absoluta, la más grande". Sin embargo, el CEO de Ducati pide calma y no 'lanzar las campanas al vuelo', pues aún quedan dos fines de semana muy importantes, especialmente en Portimao, los cuales, no sólo decidirán el Mundial de Pilotos, sino también el de Constructores, en el cual se encuentran liderando con 8 puntos sobre Aprilia. "Sin embargo, conviene recordar que el trabajo aún no ha terminado. Se necesitará una dedicación total en las dos últimas rondas, que también decidirán el importante título de constructores, para hacer honor a todo el esfuerzo realizado por el gran equipo Ducati, tanto en los circuitos como en casa, así como por respeto a nuestros rivales y a todos los aficionados", concluía Dall'Igna.

articles.title: Tom O'Brien: Jockey dies aged 39 after cancer diagnosis
articles.summary: Tom O'Brien, the nephew of trainer Aidan, rode more than 1,000 winners and won the Welsh Grand National twice.
articles.body:
Jockey Tom O'Brien has died at the age of 39 after being diagnosed with cancer.

Irishman O'Brien rode more than 1,000 winners in Britain and Ireland, including two at the Cheltenham Festival and the Welsh Grand National twice.

The nephew of trainer Aidan O'Brien, he was a mainstay of the Minehead operation run by Philip Hobbs, joining as a teenager and remaining until his retirement in 2023.

"He touched countless lives on both sides of the Irish Sea, bringing joy to everyone who had the privilege of knowing him and watching what he did best, on and off the racecourse," said British Horseracing Authority (BHA) chief executive Brant Dunshea.

"Tom was held in the highest esteem and meant so much to so many people across our sport, who benefitted from his kindness and loyal friendship.

"He will be hugely missed and his loss is immensely difficult to process.

"The racing family is distraught, but I know how we will all rally round to provide each other with support, comfort and to remember Tom as we knew him best: a brilliant jockey, a valued colleague, a loyal friend and above all a loving husband and devoted father."

Riding the Hobbs-trained Thyme Hill, O'Brien won the Liverpool Hurdle in 2021 and the Kauto Star Novices' Chase in 2022.

"It's very sad, particularly for his wife Hayley and two young children," said Hobbs, who now shares Minehead with Johnson White.

"He came to our yard from Ireland having not ridden in a race, but it soon became obvious he was pretty talented.

"He was always very reliable and a very good bloke. There's lots of good memories and there were lots of winners.

"I'd kept in touch with Tom since his retirement as he only lived half an hour away. He was only in our yard about three weeks ago."

O'Brien joined the BHA stewarding team after ending his racing career.

articles.title: Las dos caras de Aston Martin: lo que oculta la magia de Alonso en lluvia
articles.standfirst: El mejor conjunto de sábado y domingo de la temporada del AMR26 llegó en Brasil, pero existen puntos negativos... que todavía no tienen una respuesta clara
articles.summary: El mejor conjunto de sábado y domingo de la temporada del AMR26 llegó en Brasil, pero existen puntos negativos... que todavía no tienen una respuesta clara
articles.body: Con sólo un triplete por delante para terminar la campaña 2026 de la Fórmula 1, el listón de Aston Martin de cara a firmar su fin de semana más competente del año ha subido. Si bien es cierto que no sumó en el Gran Premio de Brasil, el resultado de la Q3 de Fernando Alonso y un 12º con guerra con coches del top es un balance positivo viniendo de una temporada con sólo siete puntos rescatados del 10º de Mónaco, 9º de Zandvoort y 8º de Sepang. El AMR26, que es un coche difícil, corto de evoluciones y con el peor motor, no ha permitido más, aunque en Interlagos enseñó la otra cara de la moneda. ¿Es la real? Es la cuestión. Sobre el papel se percibe a un coche vivo en la lluvia, sin padecer en cada recta (en Brasil había dos sectores difíciles) y capaz de luchar por la zona de puntos. Pero en condiciones normales aparece el otro lado que Alonso exteriorizaba: "No es divertido competir en condiciones inferiores al resto". La mezcla no ofrece más respuestas que las de un 2026 para el olvido. Fundamentalmente, Brasil cambió la triste realidad de Aston Martin. La lluvia camufló el rendimiento, especialmente desde el lado de Honda. "Las condiciones de mojado ocultan las debilidades del rendimiento del motor y los problemas de despliegue. También es importante la manejabilidad y recibimos los comentarios de los pilotos", señaló Shintaro Orihara, responsable de los asiáticos en pista. Y en pista cambió la dinámica negativa. "Con esas condiciones mejoró la competitividad. Es un rendimiento muy bueno considerando la fotografía general del año. No sumamos, pero batimos a rivales con coches más fuertes y mejores", defendió Mike Krack, su homónimo en el seno verde. Aunque les faltó el remate. Sí que la sensación fue buena, Alonso dejó el gran movimiento de la carrera en el exterior a Hamilton y el rendimiento con todos los juegos de neumáticos subió. Quizá en el muro faltó un punto más. "No estábamos seguros de la lluvia que vendría, debatíamos si habría diferencial de neumáticos o incluso llegar a una parada, pero nos dimos cuenta de que no era posible. Además, perdimos tiempo tras Piastri, llegó Norris y te ves atrapado", recordó el ingeniero de Aston sobre ese momento de dudas antes del último chaparrón. El resultado, eso sí, no limpia las heridas abiertas... ni la imagen. Que tampoco es buena pese a que la lluvia da cierto margen. No es, como si han existido casos en la historia, un coche competitivo que se rompe. Hay problemas más profundos. "Si revisamos el triplete, nos vamos con cinco abandonos en seis carreras. Lo mejor ha sido la competitividad, pero la fiabilidad es negativa", destacaba el ingeniero luxemburgués. El problema crece más porque Honda todavía tiene que encontrar sus porqués. "A mitad de curso había mejor fiabilidad y hay problemas que no solo se explican con el kilometraje o el empuje, más los de batería. Es difícil identificar el motivo y lo principal es encontrar la causa", añadió Orihara. Más allá de lo que pueda ocurrir en las últimas tres carreras, que pasarán por más penurias en las kilométricas rectas de Las Vegas y cierto espacio a la ilusión en Qatar (con altísima temperatura) o Abu Dhabi, el foco está en el futuro. Con el nuevo motor, su déficit respecto a los mejores o las evoluciones (dos) que la FIA ha confirmado que podrán presentar. Si en Sakura se ha encontrado esa fórmula en la combustión o si volverán ciertas dudas. Su discurso oficial es que existen realidades en la mesa. "También tenemos cosas positivas y hemos identificado lo que mejorar para la próxima carrera y el año que viene", argumentó Orihara. El asunto, además, es importante y lo reflejan las continuas conexiones entre Aston Martin y la cúpula nipona. Lawrence Stroll viajó a Japón, desde Inglaterra (BBC) casi se dibujaba el futuro alternativo y en Brasil también estuvo presente el CEO de la compañía, Toshihiro Nibe. Su visita se percibe como positiva. "Es bueno tener a los ejecutivos de Honda, es bueno que vean la acción en pista y creo que se irán con una sonrisa", apuntaba Krack. "Su experiencia nos ayudará a empujar en el desarrollo", cerró Orihara.

articles.title: Qatar Grand Prix was ‘right decision’ despite regional tensions: MotoGP
articles.summary: MotoGP chief says ‘it was normal that the riders showed their concerns’ but was surprised at Yamaha’s ⁠⁠⁠⁠withdrawal.
articles.body:
MotoGP’s deputy chief Carlos Ezpeleta says the ‌‌‌‌championship was right to go ahead with the Qatar Grand Prix despite rider concerns about travelling to the Gulf amid the United States-Israel war on ⁠⁠⁠⁠Iran , but added that Yamaha’s ⁠⁠⁠⁠withdrawal came as a surprise.

MotoGP had based its decision on official information from the Qatari government and from embassies with a large presence in the paddock, Ezpeleta revealed on Wednesday.

The race was postponed from April to November 6–8 due to the regional conflict, and ⁠⁠⁠⁠Ezpeleta said the event would have been cancelled or postponed again if the situation had escalated.

“We can unequivocally say that it was the right decision,” Ezpeleta told the Reuters news agency.

“Obviously, it was normal that the riders showed their concerns, and I think that we mitigated those and confronted them to the best that we ⁠⁠⁠⁠possibly could.”

“It’s just important in today’s day and age to follow official information and real intelligence versus speculation in the media and disinformation, which I think ultimately was what brought a lot of noise around the event itself.”

Several Saudi Arabian sporting events – including football , tennis , golf and cycling – were cancelled or postponed in recent weeks after attacks by Yemen’s Houthis on Riyadh’s international airport last month killed at least 12 people and wounded more than 300.

But Ezpeleta said Qatar had not been affected in the same way as its ‌‌‌‌Gulf neighbours and that planning for the race had accelerated after conditions improved in June and July.

However, Yamaha withdrew from the Qatar Grand Prix citing “company-wide travel restrictions” for the Middle East, with the factory team and the satellite team Prima Pramac not lining up on the grid, reducing the field to 18 riders.

“I can say that the decision surprised us, given the level of detail that was put into the assessment and all the planning,” Ezpeleta said.

“All the questions that Yamaha had were answered. Ultimately, Yamaha is a great partner of the championship historically, and I’m sure they will continue to be,” he added.

“We understand that it wasn’t a decision that was taken easily from their side, but it ⁠⁠⁠⁠is a decision that was surprising to us for sure.”

MotoGP had said Yamaha’s non-participation carried ⁠⁠⁠⁠sporting implications, with any consequences to be managed by FIM, the governing body of motorcycle racing.

But Ezpeleta declined to speculate on penalties.

“We just said that we would manage any contractual matters with Yamaha directly and any sporting conversations would be handled by FIM,” he said.

“We continue to say that it’s a disappointment because I think one of the strengths of ⁠⁠⁠⁠MotoGP as a championship is that all the riders, all the teams are committed for the full season,” Ezpeleta added.

“I would say as a rights holder that the teams are committed and obliged to show up at all the events and ⁠⁠⁠⁠all races.”

Yamaha and FIM did not respond to Reuters requests for comment. Yamaha’s Moto2 team ⁠⁠⁠⁠travelled to Qatar, with Izan Guevara in a close title fight and sitting second in the championship. He had a technical issue and did not finish.

The episode has also raised questions about how well MotoGP’s management communicates with riders, and Ezpeleta acknowledged the need to improve that relationship with all stakeholders.

“We have to proactively push to improve communication, especially with the teams and the ‌‌‌‌riders because they are obviously the most important part of the championship,” he said.

“We’ve been managing the sport for 35 years and we’ve had situations like this before,” Ezpeleta added, pointing to the 2011 race in Japan held after the Fukushima nuclear disaster.

“There was a lot of controversy at the time, ‌‌‌‌as ‌‌‌‌was now with Qatar, guided by misinformation and speculation, rather than facts,” he said. “We continue to say that this was the right decision.”

Aprilia’s Marco Bezzecchi won the Qatar Grand Prix, but Ducati’s sprint winner Marc Marquez finished second to establish a 60-point lead in the championship with two rounds left.

articles.title: Así vio Márquez el polémico toque con Bezzecchi: "Boom... me explotó el airbag"
articles.standfirst: En el 'Inside' de Ducati destaca un fin de semana en el que una segunda posición se celebra casi como una victoria
articles.summary: En el 'Inside' de Ducati destaca un fin de semana en el que una segunda posición se celebra casi como una victoria
articles.body: Pocas veces se ha celebrado tanto un segundo puesto. Pero para Marc Márquez suponía el acercarse casi definitivamente a su décimo título mundial de motociclismo. Podría ser campeón en el sábado de Portimao si gana la carrera corta, y por ello rompió de alegría cuando cruzó la meta del Gran Premio de Qatar. "¡Vamos!", chillaba junto a su equipo. "Fue muy dura. Muy dura. Creo que el corazón me iba a 190", añadió. Bien vale el paso gigante a una corona que viene en una de las mejores remontadas de la historia. Esos son comentarios que desvela el Inside de Ducati, el reportaje de cada Gran Premio desde el lado de los italianos. Que también toca el otro punto fundamental en Losail, el de la carrera sprint en la que se tocó con Marco Bezzecchi y ganó batiendo a un increíble Jorge Martín. Frente a las cámaras, el 93 no entra en demasiada polémica y sí señala lo que ocurrió. "En la 1 mi airbag explotó, boom...", contó. Vino de ese roce con el piloto de Aprilia que complicó una victoria dura. Pero que para el español no tiene mucho más de lo ocurrido en pista. "Podéis ver mis vueltas desde el helicóptero, siempre hago la misma línea", añadió. Más allá del contacto, el sprint aupó a Márquez durante el fin de semana para sumar el máximo de puntos entre todos los contendientes (32). "Ha sido una carrera a lo italiano, catenaccio", reconocía el catalán. Que consiguió encontrar rendimiento de una decisión arriesgada tras la bandera roja provocada por su compañero Pecco Bagnaia. "Yo probaría el blando nuevo, Marc", le recomendó Gigi Dall'Igna, gran gurú ducatista. El español hizo caso y lanzó un golpe casi definitivo al título. En domingo, Bezzecchi dio un paso más y Márquez fue a más para ser segundo en meta. "Es una gestión perfecta", repetía Davide Tardozzi, jefe del equipo oficial de Ducati. Y el piloto también valoraba positivamente a una moto que voló en rectas. "Me avergonzaba... iba 10km/h más rápido que los demás", desveló. Pero lo importante eran los puntos y unas bases claras de cara al final de curso. "Comer, entrenar y dormir", añadió el líder de MotoGP. Aunque no deja de respetar a su gran rival, Jorge Martín. "Pelea por el título y la adrenalina es la mejor anestesia contra el dolor. Además, es un piloto muy fuerte", lanzó. Como lleva pasando toda la temporada, su alegría se contrarresta con el sufrimiento de Pecco Bagnaia. El italiano empezó bien en Losail, pero una fuerte caída en el sprint, tras un contacto con Fermín Aldeguer, le envió directamente al quirófano. "Nos vemos en Portimao... o Valencia", se limitaba a decir. Lo seguro es que ya ha pasado por quirófano en Turín y decidirán si va a Portugal junto al equipo dependiendo de la evolución de los próximos días. "Es raro decir esto, pero Qatar estaba siendo uno de mis mejores fines de semana de la temporada", lanzó el italiano en sus redes sociales.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton: Ferrari's seven-time F1 world champion urges Israel to 'let the aid trucks in' to Gaza after visit to Rafah border
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton visited the Rafah border on Tuesday to witness efforts to transport aid into Gaza; Ferrari driver published Instagram post on Wednesday calling on Israel to "fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire"
articles.body:
Hamilton was in Egypt on Tuesday to witness efforts to deliver humanitarian and relief aid bound for Gaza. The Ferrari driver also toured the Rafah border crossing and visited the Egyptian Red Crescent's aid warehouses.

The US-backed ceasefire between Israel and Hamas remains in place but has not ended Israeli strikes on Gaza, while the UN World Food Programme says two-thirds of Gaza's population are struggling to get enough to eat.

Hamilton - who has previously called for peace in the region - said aid was being denied entry into Gaza for "crazy reasons".

The seven-time world champion posted on Instagram: "The past three years of Israel's genocide in Gaza is appalling.

"It's an injustice for people to be denied their freedom, their safety and their dignity. No human being should be treated as though their life matters less.

"I saw walls stretching for miles, built to keep them in. Standing there, outside what felt like an open-air prison, all I could think about was getting in to help.

"At Rafah border, I saw food trucks lined up ready to go, but they're regularly not allowed in or face major delays. The first driver in line that I spoke to had already been waiting over 12 hours.

"At the nearby logistics centre, I saw the hard work of the aid workers, but I also saw what gets rejected for crazy reasons. Sleeping bags, first-aid kits, medical equipment, wheelchairs, even footballs for kids.

"Israel needs to fulfil its obligations under the ceasefire and let the aid trucks in. No excuse.

"I know so many people feel that same helplessness. That same need to do something rather than just watch. I don't want us to get used to their suffering. I don't want us to look away."

On Wednesday, Benjamin Netanyahu, the Israeli Prime Minister, denied Israel was delaying the entry of supplies into Gaza, and blamed Hamas for the worsening conditions in Gaza, accusing them of a refusal to disarm and seizing aid for military use.

In 2021, Hamilton founded Mission 44, a charity aimed at supporting young people and improving ⁠access to education and employment ​opportunities.

He has also backed ​humanitarian and relief initiatives, and ​efforts to support people affected by ⁠conflict.

Hamilton made his visit after competing in the Sao Paulo GP last weekend, where he finished ninth. He will next compete for Ferrari in the Las Vegas GP, with Practice 1 on Friday November 20.

articles.title: ‘Malcolm in the Middle’ star, race car driver Frankie Muniz hospitalized after Daytona crash
articles.summary: Actor and race car driver Frankie Muniz was hospitalized Wednesday following a practice-lap crash at Daytona International Speedway, according to his racing...
articles.body:
DAYTONA BEACH, Fla. (AP) — Actor and race car driver Frankie Muniz was hospitalized Wednesday following a practice-lap crash at Daytona International Speedway, according to his racing team.

Team Reaume said the "Malcolm in the Middle" star was "awake and alert."

The 40-year-old Muniz was practicing for a Proud to Honor Veterans Day Classic event, a benefit race set for Wednesday night at Daytona's road course.

"We'll share updates as they become available," Team Reaume posted on X that it would provide updates when available while thanking followers for "respecting Frankie's privacy at this time."

Muniz and NASCAR driver Austin Cindric were set to represent Team Air Force in an exhibition race that benefits six nonprofits that support military and veteran communities through the Proud to Honor Fund, according to a NASCAR release.

A dozen Ford Racing drivers were split into six teams to race head-to-head in Mustang Dark Horse cars in honor of a branch of the U.S. military.

Musical performances by the Zac Brown Band, Russell Dickerson, Jo Dee Messina, Brittney Spencer, and Warren Zeiders were also part of the event.

Muniz was nominated for an Emmy and two Golden Glove Awards for his work in "Malcolm in the Middle" and was one of the best known child actors of his time. He has also appeared in films such as "Big Fat Liar," "Deuces Wild," "Agent Cody Banks" and "Racing Stripes."

According to his website, Muniz took a hiatus from the entertainment world in 2006 to pursue professional racecar driving.

He began competing in the Formula BMW USA Championship and later went on to race in the Champ Car Atlantic Championship from 2007-09. Muniz was fourth in the 2009 championship standings with two races to go before a season-ending injury resulted in multiple surgeries, the website said.

In 2024, Muniz ran 38 races each on the NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts and trucks series.

He's participated in 117 trucks series races over the last three years, with one top-10 finish at Daytona in 2025.

articles.title: El actor Frankie Muniz (Malcolm) sufre un accidente en el circuito de Daytona y es hospitalizado

articles.summary: Frankie Muniz recibió al alta hospitalaria horas después
articles.body: El actor Frankie Muniz, el protagonista de la famosa serie Malcolm (Malcolm in the Middle), sufrió un accidente con su Ford Mustang Dark Horse durante una vuelta de entrenamiento en el Daytona International Speedway mientras preparaba el 'Proud to Honor Veterans Day Classic'. El famoso intérprete de 40 años, que en 2006 se convirtió en piloto de carreras profesional, tuvo que ser hospitalizado. Poco después del accidente Team Reaume informó que "Frankie Muniz estuvo involucrado en un incidente mientras practicaba para el evento Proud to Honor de hoy en el Daytona International Speedway. Fue llevado a un centro médico local para una evaluación adicional y está despierto y alerta. Compartiremos actualizaciones a medida que estén disponibles. Gracias por su apoyo y por respetar la privacidad de Frankie en este momento". Frankie Muniz, que recibió el alta hospitalaria horas después, publicó que "me decepciona no poder participar en el evento 'Proud to Honor' de Ford. Tenía muchas ganas de honrar el servicio de nuestros veteranos y de competir contra otros pilotos increíbles". El actor y piloto profesional compartió que se siente "un poco adolorido" y que el el Mustang que conducía cumplió su función de protegerlo de sufrir lesiones más graves. "Quiero dar las gracias a todos en Ford Racing, en el Daytona International Speedway y al personal de este hospital. Quiero agradecer especialmente a todas las personas que se han puesto en contacto conmigo y por todas sus oraciones", apuntó. Frankie Muniz fue nominado a un premio Emmy y a dos Globos de Oro por su trabajo en la serie 'Malcolm in the Middle', convirtiéndose en uno de los actores infantiles más conocidos de su generación. En el mundo del cine ha trabajado en películas como Big Fat Liar, Deuces Wild, Agent Cody Banks y Racing Stripes. articles.title: La FIA da luz verde a Honda para 2027... pero también a Mercedes
articles.standfirst: El tercer periodo de revisión del ADUO no altera el orden de las fuerzas, con el mayor paquete de ayudas en Honda
articles.summary: El tercer periodo de revisión del ADUO no altera el orden de las fuerzas, con el mayor paquete de ayudas en Honda
articles.body: La Fórmula 1 llega a su recta final. En Interlagos cerró su penúltimo triplete de la temporada, dejó los títulos resueltos en favor de Kimi Antonelli y Mercedes, y encara tres citas finales en Las Vegas, Qatar y Abu Dhabi con el premio principal enfocado en las victorias de los propios Grandes Premios además de premios de consolación como el subcampeonato que vira en favor de Max Verstappen. Por ello, el 2027 gana espacio y está en mente antes de esa carrera a los test y el inicio de curso previsto para el 14 de marzo de 2027 en Bahréin. En esa carrera al nuevo curso, la F1 tendrá una carrera de desarrollo en las fábricas y hay una adicional que se centra en las unidades de potencia. Si el paso del 2025 al 2026 con las novedades fue el curso de las ventajas de la relación de compresión de Mercedes o Red Bull, hay otro elemento clave en el ADUO que permitirá evolucionar a los motoristas con las oportunidades de desarrollo adicionales. Tras la disputa de la carrera en Interlagos, la Federación Internacional (FIA) confirmó que se realizó la tercera medición del ADUO establecida hasta la cita anterior, en Austin. No hay ningún motor que tendrá una ventaja diferente de cara al inicio de 2027, con lo que se confirmó que Honda dispondrá de dos evoluciones en su unidad de potencia. Ya tenía dos en 2026 (Holanda y Madrid) y conseguirá esa homologación extra junto al juego con el límite salarial y el test con los bancos dinámicos. En clave Aston Martin, era el plan previsto que recibe la confirmación oficial. Y llegará la siguiente revisión del ADUO en el momento perfecto, con el paso a la gira europea de 2027 a partir del Gran Premio de Mónaco. "Para la primera ronda del año no estaremos con los mejores y nos hará falta dar un paso más", reconoció su ingeniero jefe en pista, Shintaro Orihara. Pero en clave competitividad, la situación de Aston Martin no será la ideal si el paso no es importante respecto a la competencia. Porque los demás motores también evolucionarán. El que se quedará igual de su unidad de potencia inicial será Red Bull PowerTrains - Ford, pues se considera como el más fuerte midiendo la parte de combustión. Pero para el resto sí habrá posibilidad de tomar las ventajas del ADUO. Es relevante el caso de Mercedes, que tiene el paquete más completo y dispondrá de otro paso más en su motor. Y en el caso de Audi o Ferrari tendrán dos evoluciones, la misma situación de Honda. Si los problemas siguen, se verán más lejos si cabe. El futuro confirmará y reordenará las fuerzas. Con el ADUO todavía muy presente. "El primer año de implementación ha reforzado nuestra creencia de que es el concepto adecuado. Es importante evolucionar para comprobar que sigue siendo eficiente, relevante y adecuado para su propósito", destacó Nikolas Tombazis, director de las categorías de monoplazas de la FIA.
